newsitem.title: UK: British businessman offers cash to Eurosceptics.
newsitem.headline: British businessman offers cash to Eurosceptics.

text.p: A British millionaire businessman said on Friday he was ready to offer campaign cash to Conservative election candidates who oppose a single European currency.

The offer by Paul Sykes, a long-time party supporter, follows reports that many Conservative candidates in the May 1 election had flouted the government's "wait and see" policy on a single currency in their personal election manifestos.
"I am an anti-federalist, I am against a single currency and a single economy in Europe," Sykes told BBC television.
"I am therefore offering candidates and MPs around the country who have already ruled out a single currency that if they are going to continue I want to help them with their funds."
Sykes was quoted in the Times newspaper as saying that he expected his offer to be taken up by a large number of Conservative candidates.
"I think the final number of candidates will be closer to 200. It is going to cost me around 500,000 pounds ($800,000). But it's worth it. The argument is moving our way," Sykes said.
The Sunday Times, in its annual list of Britain's richest people published this month, ranked electronic entrepreneur Sykes at number 73 with a fortune of 250 million pounds.
His offer came as new divisions over Europe emerged in the Conservatives.
Media reports suggested that agriculture minister Angela Browning had in an election newsletter shown clear opposition to the government's "wait and see" line on a single currency.
She denied her views differed from those of the government and the policy in the Conservative election manifesto.
